narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 69.3% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. In practical terms, it judged failure more likely than success, and that risk drove the rejection.

The strongest factor was your third-year class standing: you were in the lowest decile, while admitted students averaged around the sixth decile. That contrast pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. The second strongest factor was your first-year class standing, also lowest decile compared with an admitted-student average around the sixth decile; this also pushed toward failure. Your undergraduate grade point average of 3.00 was the third most influential factor. Although it is below the admitted-student average of 3.23, this factor actually worked in your favor, pushing the prediction toward passing rather than failing. It was not enough to outweigh the two class-standing signals. Your gender and race were not used in the prediction.

To improve a future application, ask the admissions office for specific feedback and whether additional academic work, a stronger entrance-exam score, or a revised personal statement could address the committee’s concerns. Consider retaking the entrance exam and documenting any grade trend or extenuating circumstances. Reapply only after strengthening the areas identified, especially sustained academic performance.
